ai.title: Add clean-package.js and publish hooks for manicode 1.0.9
ai.summary: Introduces clean-package.js and prepublishOnly/postpublish scripts in package.json to strip devDependencies and peerDependencies from the published tarball while preserving the local environment. The script also injects process.env.NODE_ENV = 'production' into dist/index.js to enforce production behavior. Concurrently, src/config.ts removes the custom loadEnvironmentVariables function and associated fs imports, relying instead on standard environment handling or the injected NODE_ENV. This internal cleanup reduces published package size and ensures consistent runtime configuration for the manicode CLI.

eli5.text: When a developer publishes a new version of the software to the package repository, the system now automatically strips out development-only libraries before the package is uploaded, making the downloaded package smaller and faster for end users. Before this change, anyone who installed the software got the full development dependency list bundled in; now they only get what is needed to run it. The build process also injects a production setting directly into the main script, so the software knows to connect to the live service rather than a local test environment when used by regular users.

ai.title: Use process.cwd() as project root
ai.summary: The `manicode` package updated its version to 1.0.11 and switched the `projectRoot` definition in `src/config.ts` from a static path resolution (`path.resolve(__dirname, '..')`) to dynamic execution via `process.cwd()`. This change ensures that file operations and chat storage correctly target the directory where the CLI is invoked, rather than the installation directory. `ChatStorage` and `project-files.ts` were refactored to consume the centralized `projectRoot` export, removing redundant local path calculations and constructor parameters.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant from a specific folder on your computer, it now saves your conversations and looks for your project files in that folder instead of wherever the software itself is installed. Previously, the assistant used a fixed path based on its installation location, which meant your chat history and project files might be saved to the wrong place. Now it uses the folder you're actually working in, so your conversations and files stay organized where you expect them.

ai.title: Add musings to knowledge file
ai.summary: Added three new todo items to musings.knowledge.md regarding file path context usage, server error printing visibility, and IP address configuration. These entries serve as internal tracking for potential future improvements or debugging tasks.

eli5.text: A short list of notes was added to an internal reference file, capturing three things worth keeping an eye on down the road. The notes flag that file paths might be carrying too much unnecessary context, that errors printed by the server could go unseen, and that the IP address used should come from a specific api.manicode.ai endpoint. These are reminders for the team, not changes you would notice right now, and they are already in place today.

ai.title: Rename manicode workspace to npm-app
ai.summary: Renamed the `manicode` directory to `npm-app`. Updated root `package.json` workspaces and `tsconfig.json` references to point to the new path. Internal refactor; no functional changes to the CLI or API.

eli5.text: The internal project folder previously called 'manicode' has been renamed to 'npm-app', which updates how the software's parts are organized behind the scenes without changing what the program does. Developers working on the project will see that references to the old name in configuration files now point to the new folder name, but the program itself behaves exactly as it did before. No features were added or removed, this is purely housekeeping to keep the codebase tidy and consistent.

ai.title: Disable exported tokens in project file context
ai.summary: Commented out `getExportedTokensForFiles` call in `getProjectFileContext` and wrapped function definitions in `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` with block comments. Removed unused `typescript` import. Exported tokens are now hardcoded to an empty object `{}`.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer checks what names a project's files export, so it stops spending time on that lookup. That step is now skipped entirely, leaving the project's exported-name list empty. You would not see this directly, but it trims a small bit of background work the system did when building project context.

ai.title: 1.0.13 fixes path normalization and clean script
ai.summary: Project file paths now normalize via `path.relative` instead of manual string replacement. Build `clean` script tolerates missing `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`. Adds `ssh` script for backend. Covers `npm-app` package.

eli5.text: The assistant now handles project file paths more reliably, which previously could break when figuring out which files belong to a project. It also makes the cleanup step after a build less likely to fail if a temporary file is already gone, and adds a new command to connect to a remote server for running the backend. You'd notice this if you build or clean the project locally and the process no longer errors out on missing paths or files. This is live today and only affects developers working on the project's code.

ai.title: Add Janna Stephen Windows test notes to musings.knowledge.md
ai.summary: Added Janna & Stephen test findings to musings.knowledge.md. Notes detail Windows-specific input and edit failures: backspace cursor movement, left arrow unresponsiveness, edit application errors, and CTRL-C non-functionality. Scope limited to internal documentation.

eli5.text: The team added internal notes describing what went wrong during a test session with Janna and Stephen on Windows computers. Specifically, the backspace key only moved the cursor instead of deleting text, the left arrow key did nothing, edits failed to apply even after retrying, and the standard cancel-command shortcut didn't respond. These notes were appended to an existing internal documentation page used by the development team for tracking known issues and observations.

ai.title: Rename ChatClient to Client in npm-app
ai.summary: Renamed `ChatClient` class to `Client` and `chat-client.ts` to `client.ts` within `npm-app`. Updated imports and constructor arguments in `src/cli.ts` and `src/index.ts` to reflect the new name and parameter order. Internal WebSocket property renamed from `ws` to `webSocket` for clarity. No functional changes to user-facing behavior.

eli5.text: The program now calls its helper robot by a shorter name. Internally, the software renamed the part that talks to the server from 'ChatClient' to just 'Client' and shuffled how it sets things up, but nothing you see or do as a user changed. The rename is already live and is purely housekeeping for the developers.

ai.title: Add explicit license fields to package.json files
ai.summary: Added `license: "MIT"` to `npm-app/package.json` and `license: "proprietary"` to root `package.json`. Created `README.md` clarifying that only the npm package is MIT licensed while server-side and non-public client code remains proprietary. This ensures correct license metadata is exposed for the public package.

eli5.text: The team added clear licensing information so that anyone who downloads the assistant's public toolkit knows exactly what they can and cannot use it for. The downloadable toolkit is now explicitly marked as free-to-use MIT licensed, while the rest of the project (the servers and private parts) is marked as proprietary and confidential. If you looked at the project's main description file, you'd now see a new line stating the proprietary status, and a new guidebook entry explaining that only the toolkit portion is open for public use, everything else requires explicit permission. This change is live today: the licensing facts are now clearly published and in effect, though the proprietary protections themselves existed before this update.
